subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should maintainers accept the linked PR as a scoped embedded sessions_spawn mitigation while this issue remains open for gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native follow-ups, or hold for one shared work-spawning policy seam first?
rationale: Current main is still affected, but the open candidate PR deliberately leaves meaningful spawn-capable surfaces outside its mechanical guard; automation should not choose that product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
options.body: Land the embedded sessions_spawn guard if PR review stays clean, leave this issue open, and track the remaining surfaces explicitly.

options.title: Harden Shared Policy First
options.body: Hold the linked PR until fallback-completion state is threaded through a common work-spawning policy seam that can cover OpenClaw tools consistently.

options.title: Split Upstream Codex Work
options.body: Land only OpenClaw-owned guards here and create or route a separate upstream Codex item for native spawn_agent behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
recommendation.body: Land the embedded sessions_spawn guard if PR review stays clean, leave this issue open, and track the remaining surfaces explicitly.
